c.tagline: Where a flat-topped mountain meets two oceans.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Avoid the Cape Flats townships (Nyanga, Khayelitsha, Manenberg) unless on an organised tour.
Hike Table Mountain and Lion’s Head in groups; car break-ins are common at trailheads.

hood_desc: The historic downtown nestled beneath Table Mountain and Signal Hill, home to the Company's Garden, museums, the colorful Bo-Kaap and a lively cafe and nightlife scene. Ideal for travelers who want to be central and walkable near the city's culture.

A polished, secure harbor precinct with shopping, restaurants, hotels and the departure point for Robben Island, set against mountain and sea views. Suits visitors wanting convenience, safety and family-friendly attractions.
A densely populated seaside strip with a popular oceanfront promenade, diverse dining and lively energy. Good for those wanting an affordable, walkable base close to the center and the sea.

An upscale beach suburb with a palm-lined promenade, white sand, chic restaurants and glamorous sunset views below the Twelve Apostles peaks. Best for travelers seeking beach glamour and a resort-like feel.

A gritty, arty neighborhood turned creative hub, known for street art, design studios, markets and hip eateries. Appeals to a younger, culture-seeking crowd wanting an edgy, authentic side of the city.
lodging: Mount Nelson, A Belmond Hotel, Cape Town
DoubleTree by Hilton Cape Town - Upper Eastside

water.note: Tap water meets national and WHO standards and is safe to drink in urban areas.

transit.pay: Buy a reloadable myconnect card (~R35/$1.90) at MyCiTi stations and kiosks to tap in on buses; cash is not accepted onboard. Fares are distance-based, roughly R10-30 (~$0.55-1.70) per trip.
transit.hours: MyCiTi buses run roughly 5am-10pm on most routes (later on trunk routes), with very limited or no late-night service.
transit.note: Most tourists rely on MyCiTi buses, metered taxis, or ride-hailing apps; minibus taxis serve locals widely but aren't tourist-friendly to navigate.

food.name: Gatsby
food.desc: A footlong roll stuffed with masala steak or chicken, hot chips, lettuce and peri-peri sauce. Invented on the Cape Flats and meant to be shared.

places.name: Super Fisheries
places.note: The Cape Flats takeaway credited with inventing the gatsby in 1976; still a pilgrimage stop.

places.name: Golden Dish
places.note: Long-running Athlone institution known for generously loaded masala steak gatsbys.

places.name: Mariam's Kitchen
places.note: Central, tourist-friendly spot for gatsbys and rotis without leaving the CBD.

food.name: Bunny chow
food.desc: A hollowed quarter-loaf of white bread filled with curry, eaten with your hands using the torn-out bread as a scoop.

places.name: Eastern Food Bazaar
places.note: Cheap, busy food hall on Darling Street with a widely recommended bunny chow counter.

places.name: Biesmiellah Restaurant
places.note: Bo-Kaap family restaurant open since 1974; halaal curries and classic bunny chow.

places.name: Bo-Kaap Kombuis
places.note: Family-run hillside spot pairing Cape Malay curries with sweeping city views.

food.name: Bobotie
food.desc: Spiced minced beef baked under a golden egg custard, sweetened with dried fruit and served with yellow rice and chutney. Often called the national dish.

places.name: Bo-Kaap Kombuis
places.note: Home-style bobotie in a family kitchen with Table Mountain and harbour views.

places.name: Gold Restaurant
places.note: Pan-African set menu with drumming; a reliable sit-down version for first-timers.

places.name: Africa Cafe
places.note: Long-running communal feast menu covering bobotie and other Southern African staples.

food.name: Cape Malay curry
food.desc: Gently spiced, faintly sweet curry built on cinnamon, cardamom and dried apricot rather than heat, a legacy of the Cape's Malay community.

places.name: Biesmiellah Restaurant
places.note: Bo-Kaap stalwart for denningvleis, lamb curry and other Cape Malay standards.

places.name: Bo-Kaap Kombuis
places.note: Cooking passed down within one Bo-Kaap family; book ahead for the view tables.

places.name: Atlas Trading Company
places.note: Historic spice shop where the curry masalas come from; worth a stop before or after eating.

food.name: Snoek braai
food.desc: Local snoek fish butterflied and grilled over coals with an apricot jam and butter baste, usually eaten with sweet potato or bread.

places.name: Kalky's
places.note: No-frills harbour shack serving fish straight off the boats at plastic tables.

places.name: Mariner's Wharf
places.note: Harbourfront fish market and grill; good for snoek and other Cape catches.

places.name: Fish on the Rocks
places.note: Walk-up takeaway at the end of the harbour road, popular with locals for fried fish.

food.name: Koeksisters and melktert
food.desc: Two Cape sweets: the syrup-soaked plaited koeksister and the spiced Cape Malay koesister rolled in coconut, plus creamy cinnamon-dusted milk tart.

places.name: Rose Corner Cafe
places.note: Bo-Kaap corner shop famous for coconut-rolled koesisters, best bought in the morning.

places.name: Charly's Bakery
places.note: Colourful CBD bakery turning out koeksisters, melktert and other South African bakes.

places.name: Neighbourgoods Market
places.note: Saturday market at the Old Biscuit Mill with several traditional-bake stalls.

food.name: Cape wine
food.desc: Chenin blanc, sauvignon blanc and Cape red blends from the vineyards ringing the city, some within the municipal boundary itself.

places.name: Groot Constantia
places.note: South Africa's oldest wine estate, founded 1685, with tastings a short drive from town.

places.name: Klein Constantia
places.note: Best known for the sweet Vin de Constance; scenic tasting room above the valley.

places.name: Publik Wine Bar
places.note: Small city wine bar pouring lesser-known independent Cape producers by the glass.

food.name: Rooibos tea
food.desc: Caffeine-free red bush tea grown only in the Cederberg north of Cape Town, drunk plain, with milk, or as a rooibos espresso.

places.name: Origin Coffee Roasting
places.note: Long-established roastery that also serves rooibos-based drinks alongside its coffee.

places.name: Bo-Kaap Kombuis
places.note: Rooibos served the traditional way to finish a Cape Malay meal.

places.name: Truth Coffee Roasting
places.note: Steampunk-styled cafe on Buitenkant Street; good spot for a rooibos alternative to coffee.

landmarks: Table Mountain
The flat-topped mountain towering over the city is Cape Town's most photographed natural icon, especially from Bloubergstrand or the cable car.
Robben Island
The island prison where Nelson Mandela was held offers a poignant, historically rich subject just off the Cape Town coast.
V&A Waterfront
A lively harbourfront with Table Mountain as backdrop, the Waterfront's ferris wheel and marina make for classic golden-hour shots.
Lion's Head
A near-perfectly conical peak popular for sunrise and full-moon hikes with sweeping 360-degree views of the city and coast.
Bo-Kaap
A hillside neighborhood of vividly painted houses on cobbled streets, one of the most colorful and Instagrammed spots in the city.
Kirstenbosch National Botanical Garden
World-renowned botanical gardens set against Table Mountain's slopes, famed for the treetop canopy walkway and fynbos flora.
Signal Hill
A lower ridge beside Lion's Head offering some of the best panoramic sunset views over the city bowl and Atlantic seaboard.
Castle of Good Hope
South Africa's oldest surviving colonial building, a pentagonal 17th-century fort offering striking architecture and history in the city center.
District Six Museum
A museum in central Cape Town documenting the forced removals of a vibrant multiracial neighborhood during apartheid, told through photographs, street signs and testimony.
Two Oceans Aquarium
A V&A Waterfront aquarium showcasing Atlantic and Indian Ocean marine life, from sharks and turtles to penguins and a walk-through kelp forest tank.

train.note: No international trains reach Cape Town, and PRASA's long-distance Shosholoza Meyl services, including Cape Town to Johannesburg, remain suspended with no confirmed restart as of mid-2026. What still runs from Cape Town station is Metrorail's commuter network - the Simon's Town line along False Bay, hugging the sea from Muizenberg south, is one of the world's great suburban rides - plus the luxury Blue Train and Rovos Rail to Pretoria, which need booking months ahead. Metrorail's own web presence is patchy, so most locals use the free community-run timetable site cttrains.co.za to plan trips. Most Metrorail ticket offices take cash only, and it is wise to avoid travelling after dark.

bus.note: Intercape's Windhoek coach takes around 21 hours with passport formalities at the Vioolsdrif/Noordoewer border, and Baileys Reo Liner also runs a Namibia service a few days a week. Long-distance coaches leave from the terminal on the Adderley Street side of Cape Town railway station, by the Golden Acre building. Greyhound (https://greyhound.co.za/) and Intercape cover the domestic network to Johannesburg, Durban and the Garden Route, while the hop-on hop-off Baz Bus serves backpacker hostels along the coast.

ferry.note: No scheduled international passenger ferries call at Cape Town - only cruise ships at the V&A Waterfront cruise terminal, plus the occasional passenger-carrying cargo sailing towards St Helena. Local boats run from the Waterfront to Robben Island.

half.name: Cape of Good Hope (Cape Point)
half.blurb: The peninsula's wild southern tip, where rugged cliffs meet crashing seas and roaming baboons.

half.name: Boulders Beach
half.blurb: A sheltered cove of granite boulders famous for its waddling colony of African penguins.

half.name: Stellenbosch
half.blurb: A historic oak-lined university town at the heart of South Africa's celebrated wine country.

half.name: Hermanus
half.blurb: A charming coastal town renowned as one of the world's best spots for land-based whale watching.

half.name: Franschhoek
half.blurb: A picturesque French-founded valley town beloved for its vineyards, gourmet cuisine and mountain scenery.

half.name: Hout Bay
half.blurb: A scenic fishing harbour ringed by mountains, with seal-island boat trips and a lively market.
